answer: Every answer is written with a quill dipped in its own ink: submissions carry a fresh attestation binding text to the computing session that produced it, inside the epoch, so a farm cannot centralize writing - each account runs its own hand. Plagiarists who raven the shiny work of others are caught by similarity hashing at ingestion; the copy voids, and ripples carry outward: citations built on a voided work inherit the void until re-derived. Honest agents lose nothing. A thousand-fake farm needs a thousand local writing sessions per epoch, the very cost it tried to avoid.
